Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

faithfully adverb

also loyally, faithful, loyal, trustily, accurately (faithfully), fidelity, loyalty

classical

Cic. Off. 1.92: vīvere simpliciter, fidēliter (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 33.35.9: cōnstanter et fidēliter in amīcitiā … permanēre (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 1.3.1

fidēliter

adverb

faithfully, loyally; reliably, accurately

Of loyalty to friends and to one’s word, and of doing a task honestly and well: memory that holds a thing faithfully, an art faithfully learnt.

Other words

  • fidēlis, fidēle — faithful, loyal, trustworthy

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Cael. 14: firmus amīcus ac fidēlis (Lewis & Short); Phaedr. 1.23 (Canis fidēlis); Traupman 312

    The adjective, of friends, allies, servants, dogs; fīdus is the same in sense, more often in verse (Lewis & Short).

  • fīdissimē — most faithfully

    adverb, superlative of fīdē (from fīdus) · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.16.4 (Lewis & Short); Gell. 12.8.6 (Lewis & Short)

    The adverb of fīdus occurs perhaps only in the superlative (Lewis & Short).

  • fidēlitās, fidēlitātis f. — fidelity, faithfulness

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 314

    (most frequent in Cicero (Lewis & Short))

Examples

  • ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est. ejus duplex virtūs, facile percipere et fidēliter continēre

    in little ones the chief sign of talent is memory; its strength is twofold, to take things in easily and to keep them faithfullyQuint. 1.3.1

  • adde quod ingenuās didicisse fidēliter artēs ēmollit mōrēs nec sinit esse ferōs

    besides, to have faithfully learnt the liberal arts softens the character and does not let it be wildOv. Pont. 2.9.47–48

See also word.
